A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transitional interval in the Miocene alluvium is the product of both sedimentological and post-depositional factors.

a palaeomagnetically defined reversal in alluvium is a record of local relief in the area of deposition, contemporaneous variability in rates of sediment accumulation and the post-depositional history of the sediments.
the transitional interval is a record of the time interval during which a palaeomagnetism signal is acquired, and that this time interval is controlled by the rate of sediment accumulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a high-resolution record of the palaeomagnetic record of the Siwalik rocks is a valuable archive of palaeomagnetically determined ages.
the palaeomagnetic signal in the Siwalik sediments is not necessarily a primary signal.
the palaeomagnetic record of the reversal is not a simple reflection of sedimentation.
